articles.title: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces
articles.summary: Speech brain-computer interfaces (speech BCIs) translate neural activity into language, offering a path towards restoring speech for people with paralysis and, more broadly, enabling new forms of natural human-computer interaction. Despite this promise, the field lacks a common measure of progress because systems use different datasets, recording methods, types of speech, and vocabularies, so their reported scores are rarely comparable. articles.title: SolarWM: Open Data and Scalable Training for Long-Horizon Video World Models
articles.summary: We introduce SolarWM, a fully open foundation for building interactive video world models from data preparation through long-horizon inference. Training across heterogeneous data sources and video backbones is challenging: datasets differ in temporal scale, camera geometry, visual quality, motion, and captioning styles, while video generators use distinct representations and architectures. articles.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
articles.summary: Recent web agents use world models for test-time action selection by sampling candidate actions, predicting the resulting web states, and ranking them with a ranker model or a Process Reward Model (PRM). articles.title: Repairing PBE-Spurious Metallicity for HSE06-Level Screening of 2D Photocatalysts for Green Hydrogen Production
articles.summary: Semilocal PBE calculations can remove viable photocatalysts before screening by labeling narrow-gap semiconductors as metals. articles.title: Graph Machine: Towards Better Pretraining via Edges
articles.summary: We introduce the Graph Machine (GM), an architecture that maintains an $O(n)$-sized state and accesses it through sparse, dynamic routing. Unlike methods with fixed-size states or sparse but static routing, GM preserves $O(n)$ complexity in its sparse layers without restricting the potentially accessible state size to $O(1)$. articles.title: Finite-Time Singularities of the Kähler--Ricci Flow on Fano Bundles
articles.summary: We study collapsing finite-time singularities of the unnormalized Kähler--Ricci flow on Fano bundles arising in the analytic minimal model program. articles.title: GRADSOLVE: fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles on GPUs
articles.summary: Ordinary differential equations (ODEs) underlie models in science and engineering, and many applications need derivatives of their solutions with respect to parameters. Ensembles of independent trajectories suit graphics processing units (GPUs), but current GPU software forces a trade-off: the fastest ensemble solvers cannot be differentiated in reverse mode at the speed they solve, and the solvers built for differentiation solve more slowly. articles.title: Controlling a digital twin of the CEBAF injector from EPICS
articles.summary: The Experimental and Instrumental Control System EPICS is used to control magnets and to read data from diagnostic devices in the CEBAF accelerator. We describe a prototype system where an EPICS installation, local on a laptop or Raspberry Pi, controls beam optics simulations. articles.title: Learning CNN Filters via Generalized Stein's Method
articles.summary: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have undoubtedly revolutionized image data analysis and the field of computer vision. As the cornerstone of CNNs, the convolution operation enables the networks to extract abstract features and uncover hidden relationships in the image data. articles.summary: We study Gaussian-restricted barycenters for quadratic two-sided Kullback--Leibler unbalanced optimal transport with independent marginal penalties and no coupling entropy. articles.title: When Does Authorization End? Effect Closure at Provider Boundaries
articles.summary: Revocation completion, clean state, or operation success can leave authorized work able to cause an effect the application rejects while the provider stays within its contract. articles.title: Thinking in Pictures: A Systematic Benchmark for Reasoning-driven Image Generation
articles.summary: Recent advancements in unified generative models (UGMs) and world simulators have achieved unprecedented results in visual perception and synthesis. However, these models primarily rely on surface-level event alignment, leaving the capacity for high-level visual reasoning underexplored. articles.title: Continuous data assimilation in steady Navier-Stokes equations with unknown viscosity: robust and efficient solvers and fast parameter recovery
articles.summary: Recent advances in equation discovery methods such as SINDy have highlighted the growing interest in identifying governing parameters and models directly from data. In this work, we take a complementary approach grounded in analysis and numerical PDE methods: we recover an unknown viscosity in steady Navier-Stokes equations (NSE) from partial incompressible flow observations using continuous data assimilation (CDA). articles.title: Towards Trustworthy Autonomous Robots: An Explainable AI-Based Decision Framework
articles.summary: Autonomous robots powered by deep learning face a fundamental auditability challenge: when incidents occur, investigators cannot reconstruct why the system made specific decisions. This paper presents TRACE (Transparent Reasoning Architecture for Credible Execution), a decision framework that ensures every autonomous action can be traced back to sensor evidence through documented causal chains. articles.title: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
articles.summary: Harnessing naturally occurring feedback from user interactions offers a promising learning signal for Large Language Models (LLMs). However, recent studies suggest this feedback is inherently noisy and difficult to leverage effectively. articles.title: Localized Persistent Commutative Algebra
articles.summary: We develop a localized persistent theory of commutative algebra for Stanley-Reisner rings, based on local cohomology supported at a coordinate prime rather than at the maximal ideal. articles.title: High performance Stingray
articles.summary: X-ray astrophysical objects show variability on a wide range of timescales, i.e. from fractions of second to years. The open-source Python library stingray is able to perform time series analyses with a focus on high-energy astrophysics. articles.title: The Implications of Linguistic Illegibility for LLM Security
articles.summary: LLMs are trained to generate natural language. However, various strands of evidence indicate that an LLM's externalized linguistic outputs and mechanistically-extracted linguistic features can be an unreliable lens for understanding internal model computation. articles.title: Almost Linear 3-Spanners of Temporal Cliques
articles.summary: Temporal graphs model dynamic networks by assigning positive integer time labels to the edges, while information propagates along temporal paths, whose edge labels are traversed in nondecreasing order. articles.summary: Competitive programming has become a key test of large language model reasoning, with international competitions such as IOI and ICPC representing its most challenging settings. We present an end-to-end specialization pipeline combining large-scale problem curation, synthetic reasoning traces, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL). articles.summary: Novel view synthesis from sparse inputs requires both geometric grounding from the observed views and generative priors of unobserved regions, motivating recent hybrid methods that combine reconstruction and generation. articles.title: Exponential speedup of polarization stabilization for long distance DWDM quantum networks
articles.summary: Fibre-based quantum networks distributing polarization entanglement require a stable and uninterrupted transmission basis for reliable operation. articles.title: On the equivalence of left-hand-cut and three-body formalisms
articles.summary: The "left-hand cut problem" in lattice QCD arises when exchange singularities invalidate standard relations used to extract scattering amplitudes from the finite-volume spectrum. articles.title: Efficient All-in-One Weather Restoration using Spectral Harmonization
articles.summary: Adverse weather conditions such as rain, haze, and snow significantly degrade image quality, posing challenges for both human perception and physical AI. articles.title: Non-Invariance in Nested Prediction Models under Selective Predictor Availability
articles.summary: Selective measurement of predictors is common in routinely collected health data. We used nested prediction models as a framework for characterising the consequences of a selectively measured predictor, with a restricted model defined in the target population and an extended model including the selectively measured predictor defined in a selected population. articles.title: Understanding Automatic Mixing: A Subtask-Oriented Analysis of Two-Stage Mixing System
articles.summary: Automatic mixing transforms multitrack recordings into perceptually coherent, balanced, and aesthetically consistent mixes. In real-world production, this task is challenging due to large track counts, diverse instrumentation, and strong inter-track dependencies. articles.title: Copula Transformations for Data-Consistent Inversion
articles.summary: Data-consistent inversion (DCI) constructs probability measures whose push-forward distributions agree with observed data, while iterative data-consistent inversion (iDCI) extends this framework to generalized stochastic inverse problems by enforcing multiple push-forward constraints sequentially. articles.title: Benchmarking RAW and RGB Restoration in Image Signal Processors
articles.summary: Modern cameras transform RAW sensor measurements into sRGB images through an image signal processor (ISP). We benchmark two placements for blind restoration around a fixed ISP: (A) pre-ISP restoration in the RAW domain and (B) post-ISP restoration in the sRGB domain. articles.summary: LiDAR-based semantic segmentation is a core perception module for autonomous vehicles and mobile robots. Despite the strong performance of recent state-of-the-art methods on standard benchmarks, existing evaluation protocols remain focused on clean, single-domain settings and fine-grained label taxonomies, leaving deployment readiness largely unassessed. articles.title: AI Contextual Measurement for Recovering Individual and Group-Level Effects: Validation Against Survey Measures and an Occupational Application
articles.summary: Researchers increasingly use artificial intelligence to construct measures of social, organizational, and occupational characteristics that are absent from conventional surveys. articles.title: Sharpness and critical scaling of parking
articles.summary: In the parking model, each site of the $d$-dimensional lattice independently starts with one car with probability $p$ or one parking spot with probability $1-p$. articles.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
articles.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for large language model (LLM) post-training, but its reliance on coarse outcome rewards leads to limited guidance on intermediate reasoning processes. articles.summary: A standard approach for studying magic angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG)'s correlated electronic phase diagram is to project the Coulomb interaction down to effective models only involving electrons in single-particle flat bands and some nearby remote bands. articles.summary: Text-to-image models excel at natural image synthesis but struggle with graphic design, where success depends on satisfying precise constraints on typography, layout, color, and visual communication. articles.summary: Traditional speaker-attributed ASR systems treated ASR and speaker diarization as two separate tasks.
